Neither `g{ }` nor `s{ }` has anywhere to receive it: both require their Turtle/SPARQL text to be written IN THE ldpy SOURCE, parsed when the file transpiles (querying.md) -- there is no island for 'parse whatever text a runtime variable holds', because the whole point of an island is that its content is known statically. This is not `s{ }`'s term-position `{expr}` failing to reach far enough (INSTRUCTIONS.md SS2's `-{ }`/`m{ }` limit, or region 1's algebra-rewriter finding) -- there is no query/graph literal in the source AT ALL to attach an island to; the literal-to-be-checked only exists at run time, as data.
